findings.issue_text: [BUG] The dependency-injection wiring is not updated for the changed constructor signatures: ProvideAnonymousDeviceService drops its anonStore.AnonStore parameter (replaced by sqlStore db.DB), and ProvideAnonDBStore gains a deviceLimit int64 parameter, but no wire set or wire_gen.go regeneration is included in the diff. The build breaks: pkg/wire/wire_gen.go still calls anonimpl.ProvideAnonymousDeviceService with the old argument order (it passes the *anonstore.AnonDBStore in the position now typed db.DB, a compile-time type error), and even after regeneration `wire` fails with 'no provider found for int64' because the repository has no provider for a bare int64 — the deviceLimit value must be sourced from *setting.Cfg, so the provider signature as written cannot be wired at all.

[BUG] The new code uses fmt.Errorf but the diff adds no `"fmt"` import to database.go, whose import block (context, time, db, log, sqlstore — the hunk begins at line 13, immediately after the existing imports) does not contain fmt. The package fails to compile with 'undefined: fmt'; every build including pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore fails until the import is added.

[ADVISORY] TagDevice is moved from a fire-and-forget goroutine (with its own 2-minute timeout and panic recovery) to a synchronous call inside Authenticate, so every anonymous request now blocks on the store write, and when deviceLimit > 0 additionally blocks on a full-table CountDevices query before every insert. Anonymous page loads gain the anonstore DB latency directly on the authentication hot path (previously asynchronous and non-fatal); with the limit enabled the CountDevices scan runs on every request, and any store latency or hiccup now delays or (for ErrDeviceLimitReached) fails authentication instead of being logged and swallowed as before.

[ADVISORY] The 30-day device expiration is now defined twice as two independent constants: `anonymousDeviceExpiration` in anonstore/database.go and the renamed `anonymousDeviceExpiration` (formerly thirtyDays) in anonimpl/api/api.go, with the api package's ListDevices window expected to match the store's updateDevice/CountDevices window. A future change to the expiration in one package silently desynchronizes the API's list window from the store's limit-enforcement window, producing devices that appear in the UI list but are treated as expired (or vice versa) by the device-limit logic; the next maintainer has two places to update instead of one.

[BUG] Authenticate returns the bare fmt.Errorf ErrDeviceLimitReached (created in anonstore/database.go with no errutil status mapping), so when an anonymous device over the limit authenticates, the authn service surfaces an unmapped error that renders as a 500 Internal Server Error instead of a defined 4xx/429 response. Every anonymous visitor beyond the configured limit gets an unhandled-looking 500 page on every request; there is no defined limit-reached UX or status code anywhere in the diff, and operators cannot distinguish this from a real server fault.

[BUG] AnonymousDeviceLimit is a plain int64 without omitempty, so the backend always serializes 0 when no limit is configured, making the TypeScript contract `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined` (packages/grafana-data/src/types/config.ts:200) and the `= undefined` default in grafana-runtime/src/config.ts:97 unreachable — the frontend can never distinguish 'no limit' from a limit of 0 via undefined. Any frontend consumer branching on `anonymousDeviceLimit !== undefined` to detect that the feature is configured will treat every installation as limit-bearing (value 0); the declared optional semantics are dead code and the first consumer to rely on them misbehaves.

[ADVISORY] The new `device_limit` key in [auth.anonymous] is read via MustInt64 but is added to no configuration surface in this diff — conf/defaults.ini, sample.ini, and the configuration documentation are all untouched, so the setting is invisible to operators. Operators cannot discover the feature except by reading source; default-value drift is also possible since conf/defaults.ini is the canonical place Grafana documents defaults, and it will silently disagree with the MustInt64(0) default here.

[ADVISORY] CreateOrUpdateDevice's limit check (CountDevices then insert) is not atomic, so concurrent first-visit requests on multiple instances each observe count < limit and all insert, exceeding the configured limit. On a busy multi-instance deployment the enforced device count drifts above device_limit until devices age out 30 days later; the limit is advertised as a hard cap but is only approximately enforced.

[ADVISORY] TagDevice moved from a fire-and-forget goroutine with its own 2-minute timeout into the synchronous authentication path, so every anonymous cache-miss request now blocks on a synchronous CountDevices query plus write before authentication completes. A slow or saturated database now adds latency to (or stalls) anonymous login for every user, where previously tagging failures or slowness were invisible to the request; the removed timeoutTag also means the DB call is bounded only by the request context.

[ADVISORY] The limit enforcement in CreateOrUpdateDevice and CountDevices does not filter by device kind, so renderer-tagged devices written through the same anon_device table count against the anonymous UI device limit. A deployment with heavy image rendering can have renderer devices exhaust device_limit, blocking all anonymous browser users from authenticating — an interaction no section of the change addresses or documents.

[ADVISORY] TagDevice previously swallowed tagDeviceUI failures (logged Debug and returned nil) and now returns the error, changing the contract for every caller of TagDevice, not just the anonymous authn client in client.go which filters on ErrDeviceLimitReached. Other callers that tag devices (e.g. the renderer device-tagging path) now receive raw database errors where they previously got nil, so a transient DB error that used to be a logged no-op can fail the calling flow.

[ADVISORY] No test in this diff exercises the new error path in Anonymous.Authenticate — the test-shaped files present (anonstore/database_test.go, impl_test.go) cover the store-level ErrDeviceLimitReached and TagDevice tagging, but nothing asserts that Authenticate returns the error or that non-limit tagging errors still allow anonymous authentication to proceed. A regression that accidentally swallows ErrDeviceLimitReached (silently disabling the feature) or that propagates ordinary DB errors as auth failures (breaking all anonymous logins during a DB blip) would pass CI, since this is the diff's core behavioral change on the auth path.

[ADVISORY] TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only asserts the blocked-new-device error path; the updateDevice success path — an existing device within the 30-day window being refreshed when the limit is reached — is never tested. A regression in the updateDevice WHERE clause (e.g. the BETWEEN window or RowsAffected handling) that blocks returning devices instead of refreshing them would lock out every existing anonymous visitor once the limit is hit, and no test in the diff would catch it.

[ADVISORY] The 30-day expiration constant is now duplicated: anonymousDeviceExpiration in anonstore/database.go:16 is a second hand-maintained copy of anonymousDeviceExpiration in anonimpl/api/api.go:18 (formerly thirtyDays) rather than a single shared constant. If the device expiration window is later changed in one package only, CountDevices/updateDevice in the store and the ListDevices reporting window in the API silently diverge, producing devices that are counted for enforcement but invisible in the API listing (or vice versa).

[ADVISORY] The diff publishes anonymousDeviceLimit through FrontendSettingsDTO, getFrontendSettings, and both TS config types (grafana-data/src/types/config.ts:200, grafana-runtime/src/config.ts:97) although nothing in the diff consumes it on the frontend. Server-side enforcement in anonstore is complete without this surface, so this is untraceable scope expansion: the internally-configured limit value is now shipped to every unauthenticated client in the /api/frontend/settings payload as dead data, and any future frontend consumer inherits a published contract the PR never justified.

[BUG] The PR replaces the fire-and-forget goroutine (with recover() guard and background 2-minute timeout) with a synchronous TagDevice call inside Authenticate — a hot-path behavioral change that is not required by 'add a configurable device limit'. Every anonymous authentication now blocks on the device-store write on the request path instead of proceeding while tagging happens in the background, and a panic inside TagDevice (previously recovered and logged) now propagates up through the authn flow and fails the request.

[BUG] Authenticate returns the raw ErrDeviceLimitReached sentinel (a plain fmt.Errorf with no errutil mapping), which the authn framework has no defined HTTP mapping for. Anonymous requests over the limit terminate as an opaque authentication failure (generic 500 or login redirect) rather than a defined 4xx rate-limit response, and nothing in the diff defines what the user actually sees when the limit trips.

[ADVISORY] The 30-day expiration constant is now hand-maintained in two packages — anonymousDeviceExpiration in anonstore/database.go:16 and a separate identical constant in api/api.go:18 — with no single source of truth. If the device expiration changes in one package only, the device-limit count window silently desynchronizes from the ListDevices admin window: devices would be rejected or admitted against a window different from the one operators see in the device list API.

[ADVISORY] The limit is enforced with a non-atomic CountDevices-then-insert/update sequence, not a transaction or row lock. Concurrent first-seen devices all observe count < limit and all insert, exceeding the configured limit; under HA the check is per-process against shared state, so operators configuring a hard cap get only approximate enforcement with no documentation of that slack.

[ADVISORY] The only new test exercises the limit-reached rejection path; there is no test for CreateOrUpdateDevice with deviceLimit > 0 and count < limit, nor for updateDevice succeeding for an already-known device at the limit. The two paths every real anonymous user hits when a limit is configured are unverified: a regression in the create-under-limit path (silently dropping legitimate devices) or in updateDevice's BETWEEN bounds (rejecting returning devices) would ship without a failing test.

[ADVISORY] The TS type declares anonymousDeviceLimit as `number | undefined`, but the Go DTO field is a non-pointer int64 that is always serialized (0 when the ini key is absent). The undefined branch is unreachable from the backend payload, and frontend consumers cannot distinguish 'no limit configured' from a limit of 0, so any future consumer must hard-code the knowledge that 0 means unlimited — a contract detail encoded nowhere in the types.

[ADVISORY] The new auth.anonymous `device_limit` key is read via MustInt64 but conf/defaults.ini and sample.ini are not updated anywhere in this diff. Operators get no documented, discoverable configuration entry for the feature this PR exists to deliver — the setting is only findable by reading Go source — and the documented-ini contract for auth.anonymous section settings is left incomplete.

[ADVISORY] When device_limit > 0, every cache-miss anonymous tagging performs an extra full-window CountDevices query before the write. The enforcement mechanism adds a table scan over anon_device on the exact request path the limit exists to protect, so under traffic spike conditions (when the limit matters most) each previously-write-only tagging becomes a read plus a write against the database.

[BUG] The device limit is enforced by a check-then-act sequence (CountDevices followed by the insert path) with no transaction, lock, or constraint, so concurrent first-tag requests all observe count < deviceLimit and all insert. Under any concurrency (multiple requests or multiple Grafana instances in an HA deployment), the effective device count exceeds the configured limit; a flood of distinct devices drives the count upward while every in-flight request still sees a stale sub-limit count, so the limit this feature exists to enforce is advisory, not real.

[ADVISORY] Device tagging moved from a background goroutine (with its own context.Background() + 2-minute timeout and panic recovery) into the synchronous authentication path inheriting the request context, which has no timeout. A slow or hung anonstore database now blocks every anonymous authentication (i.e., every anonymous request) for as long as the DB driver takes to time out, instead of degrading in the background as before; the previous design explicitly decoupled anonstore latency from request latency and this diff removes that boundary without adding a replacement timeout.

[ADVISORY] Every cache-miss tag of a new device performs a synchronous COUNT(*) over anon_device filtered on a 30-day updated_at window before the write, and the count result is never cached or maintained incrementally. When device_limit is configured, a flood of distinct devices (exactly the scenario a device limit targets) issues one full-window aggregate query per request in the auth hot path, making the aggregate DB work grow super-linearly with device count; the local cache only deduplicates repeat tags from the same device, not distinct devices.

[ADVISORY] Returning ErrDeviceLimitReached from the ContextAwareClient's Authenticate has no defined user-facing outcome in this diff: nothing maps the error to a response, and no test covers this branch, so whether the authn service swallows it (limit unenforced at the auth layer) or aborts authentication with a generic error is unverified. The only behavior actually verified by tests is the store-level error; if the authn framework swallows client errors the limit silently does nothing, and if it aborts, anonymous visitors over the limit receive a generic 500/401 instead of a meaningful 'device limit reached' response — and a regression flipping between these two ships green.

[ADVISORY] Device identity is client-controlled, so the limit converts a resource cap into a lockout lever: an attacker mints unique device IDs cheaply until the limit is reached, after which every new legitimate anonymous visitor is denied. Once saturated (trivial for an adversary, costly for the operator), the feature blocks all new anonymous users rather than protecting the backend; this may be the accepted trade-off of 'device limit', but the diff does not acknowledge or bound it (e.g., per-IP weighting), so it should be a conscious decision, not an emergent one.

[ADVISORY] The 30-day expiration duration is now defined twice as identically-named package-level constants — anonymousDeviceExpiration in anonstore/database.go and in anonimpl/api/api.go — with no single source of truth. The count window enforced by the store and the window the admin ListDevices API queries must stay equal for the admin UI to reflect what is actually enforced; a future edit to one constant silently diverges the two, and the second copy is exactly the kind the old thirtyDays/anonymousDeviceExpiration rename was supposed to eliminate.

[ADVISORY] updateDevice interprets RowsAffected==0 as 'device not present or stale', but on MySQL the driver reports rows changed, not matched, so a re-tag within the same second writes identical client_ip/user_agent/updated_at values (second-precision datetime) and returns 0. An existing, in-window device that tags twice within the same second across instances (bypassing the per-instance local cache) gets ErrDeviceLimitReached and its anonymous authentication fails, despite the device legally occupying one of its own limit slots.

[ADVISORY] The TS type declares anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined, but the Go DTO field is a non-pointer int64 that is always serialized, so the wire never carries undefined and 0 silently doubles as the 'no limit' sentinel. Frontend consumers must independently know that 0 means unlimited (a fact expressed nowhere in the type or name); if the Go side later switches to *int64 with omitempty, undefined starts arriving and every 0-based falsy check in frontend code changes meaning without a compile-time signal.

[BUG] The review iterations silently converted device tagging from a fire-and-forget goroutine into a synchronous call inside Authenticate, so every anonymous cache-miss request now performs inline DB work (CountDevices + upsert) before authentication can complete. The stated objective was 'add configurable device limit', but the diff also re-architected the auth path: previously tagging could never delay or fail authentication; now each new device's first request in a 15-minute window pays the full store round-trip inline, and any store slowness directly inflates anonymous request latency — an objective change with no explicit acceptance anywhere in the PR.

[BUG] Deleting the goroutine also deleted all three of its isolations at once: the detached context.Background, the dedicated 2-minute timeout, and the recover() guard, so TagDevice now runs on the cancelable request context with no panic barrier. Two concrete regressions: (1) a client that disconnects mid-request cancels the request context, which now aborts the device write that was previously designed to survive disconnects; (2) a panic inside TagDevice/anonstore propagates out of Authenticate into the authn middleware, turning what was a logged 'Tag anon session panic' warning into a failed request.

[BUG] The added `return err` makes TagDevice propagate every tagDeviceUI failure to all callers, where the previous contract (and everything the device-limit feature needs) only requires propagating ErrDeviceLimitReached. Transient store failures during device tagging change from logged-and-ignored to error returns across every TagDevice call site, including the post-auth hook path outside this diff, silently tightening the error contract of a public service method without the feature requiring it.

[BUG] The `thirtyDays` constant — previously only the API listing window — was silently repurposed and renamed into `anonymousDeviceExpiration`, a hardcoded security-enforcement parameter, while the device rows themselves are only cleaned up after 61 days. Once the limit is reached, a returning anonymous user whose device row was last updated more than 30 days ago (rows persist up to 61 days per DeleteDevicesOlderThan) fails the `updated_at BETWEEN` guard in updateDevice, matches 0 rows, and gets ErrDeviceLimitReached — so legitimate returning users are locked out of authentication and their stale slots can never be reclaimed until the 61-day cleanup runs. The PR promises a 'configurable device limit' but the enforcement expiration is a hardcoded repurposing of an unrelated display constant, never accepted as part of the objective.

[BUG] When the limit is reached, Authenticate returns `nil, ErrDeviceLimitReached` where ErrDeviceLimitReached is a bare fmt.Errorf with no HTTP-status mapping, so a 'limit reached' condition surfaces to new anonymous devices as a generic failed authentication rather than a 429/403-class response. Every new anonymous device after the limit is hit receives an unmapped internal error path from the authn layer; operators enforcing a device limit get bug reports about mysterious auth failures instead of a meaningful rate-limit signal, and nothing in the diff maps the sentinel to a client-appropriate status.

[ADVISORY] AnonymousDeviceLimit is added to FrontendSettingsDTO without omitempty, broadcasting the anonymous-device limit configuration to every client including unauthenticated ones, and nothing in the diff consumes it on the frontend. Anonymous visitors learn the exact device limit (and that limit enforcement exists) from the settings payload, while the added TS field has no reader in this diff — a ships-inert public exposure whose only present effect is information disclosure about the abuse-control configuration.

[ADVISORY] The TS type declares `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined`, but the Go DTO serializes int64 with no omitempty, so the wire always carries a number and `undefined` is unreachable. Frontend code cannot distinguish 'no limit configured' from 'limit = 0', which are different semantics in the backend (0 means unlimited); any future frontend consumer keying off the `undefined` branch will silently misread unlimited as a zero-device limit.

[ADVISORY] The limit check is a non-atomic count-then-insert: concurrent first-seen devices all read the same CountDevices result below the limit and all proceed to insert. Under a burst of new anonymous devices the stored device count overshoots the configured limit, so the delivered enforcement is best-effort — silently weaker than the 'device limit' guarantee the PR title states, and surprising for operators who configure the limit as a hard cap.

[ADVISORY] The most consequential new behavior in the diff — anonymous authentication being rejected once the device limit is reached — has no test anywhere in this change. The only new test exercises the store returning ErrDeviceLimitReached; a regression in the errors.Is dispatch, the nil-identity return, or the swallow-vs-block split in Authenticate would silently flip between 'anonymous access blocked' and 'anonymous access unbounded' with no failing test, on the exact behavior the PR exists to deliver.

[BUG] The device limit is enforced against client-asserted device identities with no rate limiting or cleanup of attacker-created entries, so an unauthenticated client can fill the limit and lock out all new anonymous users. An attacker scripts requests that omit or rotate the anonymous device cookie; each request creates a new anon_device row via CreateOrUpdateDevice (the upsert path at line 108-118 counts and accepts them until count >= deviceLimit). Once the limit is reached, every new device_id fails updateDevice (0 rows affected) and receives ErrDeviceLimitReached from Anonymous.Authenticate, denying anonymous access to all new legitimate visitors. Because entries only age out via the 30-day anonymousDeviceExpiration window, a cheap one-time flood blocks new anonymous sessions for up to 30 days with no administrative remediation path added in this diff.

[ADVISORY] The limit enforcement is a count-then-act check with no transaction or lock, so concurrent first-tag requests can push the device count past the configured limit. Two concurrent requests each run CountDevices while count == deviceLimit-1, both see headroom, and both take the insert path, exceeding the limit. Operators relying on device_limit as a hard capacity cap (e.g. for license-like or load reasons) get a soft limit that leaks under concurrency, and the overshoot persists for the 30-day retention window. A single transaction with a locking read or an atomic conditional insert would close the gap.

[ADVISORY] TagDevice moved from a panic-recovered, timed-out goroutine to a synchronous call in the authentication path, so any panic or slow DB round trip in tagging now fails or delays authentication instead of being contained. The removed defer/recover block previously contained any panic in the tagging path; now a panic inside TagDevice/the anonstore propagates out of Authenticate into the authn middleware, turning a background nuisance into a per-request 500 for anonymous users. The removed 2-minute context.WithTimeout also means a hung DB session (e.g. lock contention on anon_device under the new UPDATE-heavy path) blocks the request rather than the goroutine, adding tagging latency to the authentication critical path on every cache miss.

[ADVISORY] anonymousDeviceExpiration is defined identically in two packages (anonstore/database.go line 16 and anonimpl/api/api.go, replacing thirtyDays), creating a parallel hand-maintained constant pair. The store's updateDevice window and the API's ListDevices fromTime must stay in lockstep for the device list and the limit enforcement to agree on what counts as an active device; when expiration is next changed (e.g. made configurable, which the config plumbing in this diff invites), updating only one definition silently makes the admin device list and the limit counter disagree about which devices are active. Exporting the constant from anonstore and consuming it in api removes the second place to update.

[ADVISORY] updateDevice's WHERE device_id = ? matches any row for a client-supplied device identifier with no binding between the cookie value and the client that created it, allowing arbitrary anon_device rows to be rewritten. The device_id originates from a client-held cookie; nothing in this diff validates its format or ownership. A client that sets the device cookie to another device's id can, once the limit is active, overwrite that row's client_ip, user_agent, and updated_at (keeping an arbitrary device perpetually inside the retention window or polluting the IP/UA data operators see in the device list). Impact is limited to anonymous telemetry data, but the limit mechanism itself is what creates the new write path over foreign rows.

[ADVISORY] TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit exercises only the reject branch of the new limit flow: it never invokes the updateDevice success path (count >= limit with a device_id that has an existing in-window row, rowsAffected > 0) and never asserts persistence state with ListDevices. A regression in updateDevice's WHERE/SET clause — e.g., the BETWEEN window matching the wrong rows, or client_ip/user_agent/updated_at written with stale values — or a regression where the limit branch silently skips storage entirely would all pass CI, because the test's only assertion is require.ErrorIs on the sentinel returned for a device_id with no row; the production 'returning anonymous device keeps working at the limit' guarantee, which is the core user-facing behavior of this feature, is unverified.

[ADVISORY] The new error-return branch in TagDevice (previously tagDeviceUI failures were logged and swallowed) has no test coverage: impl_test.go's changes in this diff are signature updates only, and every case in TestIntegrationDeviceService_tag and TestIntegrationAnonDeviceService_localCacheSafety calls TagDevice on the happy path and asserts require.NoError. If this branch regresses to swallowing the error again, ErrDeviceLimitReached never reaches client.go's Authenticate and the device limit silently stops enforcing — the suite still passes; conversely, if TagDevice starts propagating non-limit errors that Authenticate handles via the same errors.Is-miss path, no test in the diff distinguishes it.

[ADVISORY] This diff introduces a second package-private constant with the same name and value, anonymousDeviceExpiration, in anonstore/database.go (line 16) and api/api.go (line 18), replacing the previous single thirtyDays constant, with no shared source of truth. The next engineer who changes the device expiration window must find and update two constants in two packages; if only one is changed, the device-listing/reporting window in ListDevices diverges from the window used for limit counting and stale-device rejection in updateDevice, producing devices that appear in the UI list but are not counted (or vice versa) — and no test asserts the two windows agree.

[ADVISORY] The device expiration constant is now defined independently in two packages: `anonymousDeviceExpiration = 30 * 24 * time.Hour` in anonstore/database.go and an identically-named constant in anonimpl/api/api.go (renamed there from `thirtyDays` in this diff), with no shared source of truth. The api.go copy governs the ListDevices API query window while the database.go copy governs the limiter's CountDevices and updateDevice windows; when someone tunes the expiration in one package only, the devices shown in the UI silently diverge from the devices the limit counts and the update window accepts, and nothing in the code links the two definitions to surface the drift. api.go already imports the anonstore package (it uses anonstore.Device and anonstore.AnonStore), so importing a single exported constant there removes one of the two places to update at zero cost.

[BUG] Authenticate returns the raw anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached sentinel to the authn layer, which has no classification for it, so over-limit anonymous devices are rejected with a 500-class internal-error response instead of a defined 4xx. Every request from a device at the limit (the normal steady state once the cap is hit) fails with an internal-server-error shape; operators see 500 spikes and clients cannot distinguish 'capacity reached' from a Grafana malfunction.

[BUG] The device limit is enforced with a non-atomic count-then-insert: concurrent first-seen devices all read count < deviceLimit and each proceeds to the INSERT path, exceeding the configured limit. Under concurrent traffic (e.g., a burst of new visitors when count == deviceLimit-1), multiple inserts race past the check and the table ends up above the configured cap; the limit the feature promises is not actually enforced exactly when it matters (load spikes).

[ADVISORY] TagDevice was moved from a fire-and-forget goroutine (with its own 2-minute timeout context and panic recovery) to a synchronous call on the request's context with no timeout, adding two blocking DB round-trips (CountDevices + upsert) to anonymous authentication on every local-cache miss. A slow or saturated database now directly inflates or stalls every anonymous request's authentication path instead of degrading only background tagging; the previous design isolated this latency (and its 2-minute cap) from the request, and that isolation was removed without a replacement timeout.

[ADVISORY] The 30-day device expiration window is now defined twice as independent constants in two packages (anonymousDeviceExpiration in anonstore/database.go and in api/api.go) that must stay in sync with each other and with the count window in CreateOrUpdateDevice. The next change to the device retention window that updates only one copy silently desynchronizes the ListDevices API window from the limit-enforcement count window, producing devices that are visible to the API but not counted (or vice versa) with no compile-time signal.

[ADVISORY] device_limit is read with MustInt64(0) and the store treats any value <= 0 as unlimited (deviceLimit > 0 guard), so a negative or typo'd config value silently disables the limit with no validation error or log. An operator who sets device_limit = -1 (or another negative) intending to cap devices gets unlimited device rows with no startup warning, and the table grows unbounded until the 61-day cleanup prunes it.

Anonymous authentication now fails entirely if anonDeviceService.TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. Previously, device tagging was asynchronous and non-blocking. This change prevents anonymous users from authenticating when the device limit is reached.
The updateDevice function returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when rowsAffected == 0, but zero affected rows means the device doesn't exist or falls outside the time window, not that a limit was reached.

Time window calculation inconsistency: Using device.UpdatedAt.UTC().Add(-anonymousDeviceExpiration) as the lower bound but device.UpdatedAt as the current time may not match the intended logic. Consider using time.Now().UTC() consistently.
